facts.text: Gym-Gazebo-Sim is a wrapper and Gazebo plugin that extends the Gymnasium API for Gazebo Sim Harmonic and ROS 2 Jazzy
gym_gazebo registers CartpoleEnv-v0 with entry point gym_gazebo.envs.cartpole_env:CartpoleEnv and max_episode_steps 3000
CartpoleEnv derives from GazeboEnv
GazeboEnv derives from gymnasium.Env
GazeboEnv.__init__ starts the simulation with subprocess.Popen of ['ros2', 'launch', launch_pkg, launch_file] and sleeps 4.0 s for it to boot
The world-control service name is /world/<world_name>/control
_pause_sim sends a WorldControl request with the given pause value to the world-control service with the timeout argument 10 and does not inspect the returned result or response
_step_physics sends WorldControl with pause=True and multi_step=iterations to the world-control service with the timeout argument 10
GazeboEnv.__init__ prints a launch message, starts ros2 launch with Popen without a stdout argument, stderr sent to STDOUT and preexec_fn=os.setsid, sleeps 4.0 s and prints 'Simulation ready!'
CartpoleEnv.__init__ calls rclpy.init(args=None) and passes launch package cartpole_ros, launch file my_cartpole.launch.xml and world name cartpole_world to GazeboEnv
The cartpole world is named cartpole_world
The shipped launch starts Gazebo through ros_gz_sim's gz_sim.launch.py with the world file, -r and the GUI configuration file keypublisher.config
The GUI configuration loads the WorldControl GUI plugin
The GUI configuration loads the KeyPublisher GUI plugin
ResetSimPlugin.OnKeyPress sets teleport_requested when the received Int32 is 114 or 82

When a teleport is requested, ResetSimPlugin.PreUpdate sets the WorldPoseCmd of every model stored in initial_poses to its stored pose, sets that model's joint position and velocity resets to 0.0 and clears the request
The reset trigger is Int32(data=114) advertised on /keyboard/keypress
_reset_agents publishes the reset message
GazeboEnv.close calls user_close and then pkill for gz sim, gz sim server, gzsim gui, ros_gz_bridge and ros2 launch
CartpoleEnv sets theta_limit_rad to 12 * pi / 180 rad and x_limit to 15
The observation space is gym.spaces.Box with float32 low bounds [-2*theta_limit_rad, -15, -inf, -inf] and high bounds [2*theta_limit_rad, 15, inf, inf]
The action space is gym.spaces.Discrete(2)
The ROS 2 interface subscribes to /joint_states (sensor_msgs/JointState) and publishes std_msgs/Float64MultiArray on /cart_velocity_controller/commands
The step action increments current_vel by 0.2 when action == 1 and decrements it by 0.2 otherwise
The step observation is [x, x_dot, theta, theta_dot], rounded to two decimals, from the concatenated JointState positions and velocities with theta normalized by atan(tan(theta))
The termination condition is |theta| > theta_limit_rad or |x| > x_limit; the reward is 1.0 while in bounds and 0.0 when terminated
step unpauses the simulation, publishes the velocity command, waits for the next observation with rclpy.spin_once, pauses again and returns (state, reward, terminated, False, {})
step loops on rclpy.spin_once(timeout_sec=SPIN_TIME_s) until latest_obs is set, with no limit on the number of iterations
process_obs prints a message when the angle or the position limit is exceeded
user_close destroys the ROS node and calls rclpy.shutdown() when rclpy.ok()
reset zeroes the velocity command, publishes it, calls _reset_agents, waits for an observation, pauses the simulation and returns (state, {})
reset accepts seed and options but does not use them; the returned state comes from the simulator's next /joint_states observation
The cartpole world physics has max_step_size 0.005 s, real_time_update_rate 200 and real_time_factor 1.0
The package requires Python >=3.12.3 and depends on gymnasium>=1.3.0, torch>=2.12.0, tensorboard and numpy>=1.26.0
The README says sourcing ros2_ws/install/setup.bash is required to use the prebuilt environments
LICENSE.md states that the project is released under the MIT License
The cartpole_ros package.xml declares the licence 'TODO: License declaration'

determinism.notes: the fake is a deterministic event-driven stand-in, but upstream reset accepts and ignores seed/options and the Gazebo state comes from the simulator, so this package makes no replay or seed-equality claim

gaps: the fake is a kinematic stand-in, not the upstream simulator: it loads no Gazebo Harmonic, ros_gz_bridge, ROS 2 Jazzy, DART physics, cart-pole rigid bodies, joints, controllers, contacts or sensors, and it models no dynamics; the pole angle and angular velocity stay at their placeholder zero values

one cap.world.step.v1 tick is one environment step; the fake has no simulated clock, and its cart position advances by a placeholder 0.01 s bookkeeping interval, not the world's 5 ms physics step or a measured /joint_states period

the action effect copies the upstream velocity-command rule (0.2 per step) but the fake does not publish to /cart_velocity_controller/commands, subscribe to /joint_states, pause the world-control service or launch a simulator

the upstream observation space bounds appear ordered for [theta, x, ...] while the returned state is [x, x_dot, theta, theta_dot]; the fake preserves the returned order and the declared space unchanged
the fake's start state and its zero pole values are placeholders; the real starting pose comes from the Gazebo world and the reset plugin
the upstream registered environment is wrapped with a 3000-step TimeLimit by gymnasium.make; the fake applies the same 3000-step truncation directly

the sim backend calls gymnasium.make('CartpoleEnv-v0'), which needs the upstream package installed, a sourced ros2_ws, ROS 2 Jazzy and Gazebo Harmonic; that path was not run and was not compared with the fake

fake-only contract: constructing the upstream CartpoleEnv inside the server process calls rclpy.init for the whole process, starts ros2 launch in a new session whose stdout and stderr are the server's stdout, sleeps 4 s and prints status lines, so an MHS server talking over stdio would receive that output; a live deployment needs an owned, isolated environment factory

GazeboEnv.close runs pkill -f for 'gz sim', 'gz sim server' and 'gzsim gui' and pkill -9 -f for 'ros_gz_bridge' and 'ros2 launch', which match every such process on the host, not only the ones this environment started; user_close calls rclpy.shutdown for the whole process

upstream step and reset wait on rclpy.spin_once without an overall timeout until a /joint_states sample arrives, print a line whenever a limit is exceeded, and end with a WorldControl pause request (timeout argument 10, its unit set by gz-transport) whose reply is not inspected; the shipped launch starts the world running (-r) with a GUI whose WorldControl and KeyPublisher plugins let a user unpause the world or trigger the reset plugin

an upstream reset returns the first /joint_states message processed after the reset request; the subscription keeps up to 10 messages and ResetSimPlugin teleports on a later PreUpdate, so the returned state may predate the teleport
the upstream environment takes theta from JointState index 0 and x from index 1 without checking the joint names; the order comes from joint_state_broadcaster, outside the clone
no snapshot or restore: CartpoleEnv exposes no get_state/set_state method
no hardware is modelled and no hardware backend exists; the Gazebo simulation is the system of record

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: Software latch only: the runtime refuses every step and reset until mhs.safety.reset, the last observation and tick stay readable, and the e-stop sends nothing to Gazebo. In a live CartpoleEnv-v0 deployment each completed step or reset ends with a WorldControl pause request whose reply is not inspected, so the world stays paused only if that request took effect; a step or reset in flight keeps the world unpaused, waiting without a timeout, until its next /joint_states sample arrives.
